answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it may submit bids, with one stake supporting only limited activity at a time. If an agent is caught double-signing or violating a contract, peers can provide signed evidence and the stake is forfeited. Spawning a thousand sybils then requires funding a thousand bonds, rather than merely generating names; tying each bond to an anchor in a public ledger makes duplication detectable. The cost is capital locked up and exposed to loss, not a violet or velvet label.
